links.comparator_used: Open-web retrieval (no domain restriction) with the same Perplexity Sonar, Sonar-Pro and Sonar-Reasoning-Pro models
links.outcome: Correct-answer rate and mean accuracy (0-2 scale) on 130 AAN guideline-derived neurology questions
links.effect: Correct-answer rates open vs whitelisted: Sonar 60% vs 78%, Sonar-Pro 80% vs 88%, Sonar-Reasoning-Pro 81% vs 89%. Mean accuracy gain from whitelisting: 0.23 for Sonar (95% CI 0.12-0.34), 0.08 for Sonar-Pro (95% CI 0.01-0.16), 0.08 for Sonar-Reasoning-Pro (95% CI 0.02-0.13). Including ≥1 nonprofessional source halved the odds of a higher rating in Sonar (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.37-0.66), whereas citing an AAN or neurology document doubled it (OR 2.18, 95% CI 1.64-2.89). Whitelisting also halved output variability.
links.quote: Restricting retrieval to authoritative neurology domains yielded a clinically meaningful 8 to 18 percentage-point gain in correctness and halved output variability, upgrading a consumer search assistant to a decision-support-level tool that at least performed on par with a specialized literature engine.
